name: Nick León
label: TraTraTrax
lede: A Fruity Loops kid from Fort Lauderdale sold beats to Miami rappers, burned out on the European festival circuit, and came home to make the record Pitchfork called a dembow pop album for muggy, electric nights.

eras.title: A borrowed copy of FruityLoops, then Miami rap
eras.text: Born in California and raised in Fort Lauderdale, León learned production in his bedroom and sold beats to South Florida rappers before anyone called him a club artist. His first album already leaned toward the dystopian club sound he kept refining.

years.h: A borrowed copy of FruityLoops, a DatPiff account
years.p: Nick León, born in Oakland and raised in Fort Lauderdale from age 3, started making beats at 12 on his older brother's software and posted them to DatPiff.
years.xp:
Miami New Times reports he borrowed FruityLoops from his older brother, made beats for high school classmates and, after graduating, studied audio engineering at the SAE Institute. He also interned at the former Lenny Kravitz studio at the Setai hotel.

He told Remezcla that the mid-2000s reggaeton boom from Puerto Rico and Colombia shaped his ear, and that Flying Lotus and Aphex Twin made him question what he thought he knew about music.

years.src: Remezcla · Miami New Times · Resident Advisor: Nick León biography
years.h: León's beats end up under Denzel Curry and Robb Bank$
years.p: Remezcla credits him with Curry's "ULT" and Robb Bank$'s "Pressure", both with millions of SoundCloud plays.
years.xp: Miami New Times lists Sndngchllz and Twelve'Len among the South Florida acts he also produced for. Resident Advisor's bio says he came up working with underground South Florida rappers before moving into electronic production.

years.h: From rap beats to a solo debut on Alpha Pup
years.p: Profecía came out on the Los Angeles label Alpha Pup, with tracks like "Jaguar Sun" and "Eclipse".
years.xp:
AllMusic dates Profecía to 2016 and calls it his experimental club debut. Around the same time he founded Space Tapes, a label meant, per Miami New Times, to push left-field Miami acts.

Remezcla caught him mid-shift: harder beats giving way to ambient textures, with Colombian instruments (cuatro, marimba) borrowed from his family.

eras.title: Mexico City calls, and one rave track changes the job
eras.text: Two labels in the Latin club underground took him in. Then one track turned a Miami beat-maker into a touring act, and pop stars started phoning.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Nick León biography · Mutek
years.h: Aguacero puts a Miami producer on Mexico City's NAAFI
years.p: The EP landed León on the Mexico-based label at the center of the post-club Latin scene, and pointed his sound at Florida's storms and swamp.
years.xp: Resident Advisor's biography credits the NAAFI release and describes his music as dystopian club music informed by Florida's natural sounds. Mutek lists it alongside Rompediscoteka (TraTraTrax, 2021) as the run that set up his breakout.

years.src: First Floor · Futurism Restated · Resident Advisor: Nick León biography
years.h: "Xtasis" with DJ Babatr is the track everyone names in December
years.p: Resident Advisor and Crack both picked it as track of the year, and tastemakers started looking at Miami dance music again.
years.xp:
First Floor reports both outlets' year-end honors. Futurism Restated says León almost held it back and that label partner Verraco talked him into releasing it. Resident Advisor lists remixes by Doctor Jeep and Pearson Sound on the EP.

He signed with a European agency and, per the same interview, started his first continental tour that fall, playing festivals for roughly the next year and a half.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Nick León biography · Futurism Restated
years.h: Rosalía's Motomami credits León as a producer
years.p: Resident Advisor's biography lists production work on her 2022 album; the exact tracks aren't in the sources we could open.
years.xp: Futurism Restated places the Rosalía work and the release of Xtasis in the same 2022 window as the moment his career changed shape. We could not verify exact track credits from the sources we could open.

eras.title: Burnt out, then underwater
eras.text: Constant touring wore León down and left Miami feeling like somewhere he no longer lived. The way out ran through Brazil, Ecuador, a sea-level-rise concept album and a duet with a Danish singer.

years.big: "I don't hate dance music. I've just been in Europe for too long."
q: I don't hate dance music. I've just been in Europe for too long.
years.h: Home from Europe, burnt out, contracts cancelled
years.p: After a run of festivals and a New York show, Nick León cancelled contracted dates for the first time and went to Brazil and Ecuador to reset.
years.xp:
In a June 2025 Futurism Restated interview he said he was "very much not taking care of myself" and fully burnt out. He described two years of touring without staying 17 days in one place, and Miami gentrifying while he was away.

Watching local DJs in Brazil and Ecuador, he realized he had been forcing dembow rhythms to fit what he thought European crowds wanted.

years.h: A flooded Miami, scored with Coral Morphologic
years.p: Projections of a Coral City pairs León with the Miami marine-biology art duo on Balmat: ambient, and built as climate fiction.
years.xp: Futurism Restated describes the record as speculative climate fiction imagining a flooded Miami. AllMusic dates it 2024.

years.h: Resident Advisor calls "Bikini" the best track of 2024
years.p: Nick León's duet with Erika de Casier also drew praise from Pitchfork and The Guardian, per Mutek.
years.xp: Futurism Restated calls it a summer anthem. It later closed A Tropical Entropy as track 11, and Resident Advisor's review called it his breakout hit.

eras.title: A Tropical Entropy
eras.text: León made his first proper album about home: decaying, colorful, sleepless South Florida. Pitchfork ranked it No. 20 among the best albums of 2025.

years.h: Barcelona, then a songwriting camp, days before the album
years.p: Nick León played the Nitsa stage at Primavera Sound and joined a UMPG Spain camp at John Talabot's Angel Sound Studios.
years.xp: Futurism Restated reports he shared the Nitsa bill with RHR, Nicolá Cruz and Miami's INVT collective.

years.src: Album of the Year · Resident Advisor: Nick León · Bandcamp: A Tropical Entropy · Futurism Restated
years.h: Eleven tracks about Miami coming apart
years.p: Pitchfork gave A Tropical Entropy 8.3 (83/100 per Album of the Year) and ranked it No. 20 of 2025. Guests include Ela Minus, Jonny From Space and Erika de Casier.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's blurb, as quoted by Album of the Year, calls it a dembow pop record made for muggy, electric nights. Resident Advisor's Jake Indiana called it far and away the strongest of León's releases and singled out "Ghost Orchid" and "Broward Boyy". Album of the Year also lists it at No. 43 on Stereogum's list and No. 25 on Crack's.

León says it draws on Joan Didion's book Miami. The Bandcamp page lists Xander Amahd, Esty, Mediopicky, Lavurn and Casey MQ as guests and names tracks like "Metromover" and "R.I.P. Current". It came out on TraTraTrax, the label of "Xtasis".
